messages:
sara: noticed host CPU noise on preparse during the 8am traffic surge. short streams affected.

nick: any correlation with last night's kernel-picker rollout?

sara: yes, hosts in the picker cohort show +2x syscalls. pprof points to parse::request_unmarshal and socket_writev. kvcache fine.

omar: could be small write path again. we changed the kernel to vec-io variant which disables coalesce in proxy config via a kernel flag.

kai: timeline: kernel-picker rolled at 02:15, mini-batch scheduler also toggled prefork. Both could combine.

sara: quick experiment: toggled coalesce_small_writes=true locally and syscall rate drops ~45%. Also tried minidecode short-circuit and saw tokenizer CPU drop ~30%.

nick: plan: 1) enable coalesce on canary 2) short-circuit minidecode for <=12 tokens 3) drop prefork to 2 threads 4) add metrics for write sizes and preparse syscall rate.

omar: watch for side effects: coalescing can increase latency for first-byte in some streaming modes. ensure we flush on first chunk for streaming requests.

kai: good call. we'll implement a size-or-time flush (max 1KB or 5ms).

sara: will create canary groups. also add a guard in kernel-picker to avoid selecting vec-io for median_io < 64 bytes.

sre-bot: canary scheduled: coalesce=true on group canary-w1 (10%).

sara: thanks. will post telemetry in 40m.
